name: SIGMA - MSHTA Execution With Suspicious Extension or Inline VBScript
author: Diego Perez (@darkquassar), Markus Neis, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems) (original rule), Yohan Landji (Cyberlandji) (PB-02 adaptation)
description:
Detects mshta.exe executing an inline HTA that carries VBScript, or referencing a file whose
extension is not typical HTA content (often a polyglot). mshta is a signed Windows LOLBin;
adversaries proxy execution through it to evade process-name allowlists. Emulated as Magpie
node 2 (Atomic Red Team T1218.005 test #10): cmd.exe launches mshta.exe with an about: inline
HTA whose VBScript spawns powershell.exe. Defender AV already detects and removes this node
(Trojan:Win32/ClickFix.DJS!MTB) - this rule is defense-in-depth, keying on the process-creation
start event, which persists despite Defender's later remediation.
false_positives: False positives depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\mshta.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:mshta.exe) AND (process.command_line:(*.7z* OR *.avi* OR *.bat* OR *.bmp* OR *.conf* OR *.csv* OR *.dll* OR *.doc* OR *.gif* OR *.gz* OR *.ini* OR *.jpe* OR *.jpg* OR *.json* OR *.lnk* OR *.log* OR *.mkv* OR *.mp3* OR *.mp4* OR *.pdf* OR *.png* OR *.ppt* OR *.rar* OR *.rtf* OR *.svg* OR *.tar* OR *.tmp* OR *.txt* OR *.xls* OR *.xml* OR *.yaml* OR *.yml* OR *.zip* OR *vbscript*))
